finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.assumptions: The variable ticksPerSecond is attacker-controlled or can be influenced by user input, and it is used to control the tick rate and update the elapsed time.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that ticksPerSecond is defined as a hard‑coded constant on line 57 and never derived from untrusted input. Confirmed that the only operations involving ticksPerSecond are arithmetic updates of elapsed time (lines 109‑112) and loop control. No OS command or system call is invoked anywhere in the code. Therefore there is no path from an untrusted source to an OS command execution sink.

finding.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
finding.trigger: ability1.damagePerTick or ability2.damagePerTick is very large
finding.assumptions: The damagePerTick values are attacker-controlled or can be influenced by user input, and they are used directly to reduce the dummy's health.

parsed.refutation_attempt: No untrusted source: damagePerTick is hard‑coded in main (lines 24–26 and 55–56). Thus there is no path from attacker input to the sink.

finding.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
finding.trigger: activationCooldown is set to a hardcoded value
finding.assumptions: The activationCooldown variable is hardcoded and not configurable, which might lead to predictable behavior.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The variable activationCooldown is an internal simulation timer, set to the constant value 1.0 on line 62 and reset to 1.0 on line 88. It is never derived from any external input (stdin, file, network, argv, environment variables, IPC, or public API parameter). Therefore it does not constitute untrusted data and cannot be considered a credential. The sink on line 111 simply decrements this internal counter by a derived value (1.0 / ticksPerSecond), which is a benign arithmetic operation. No security-sensitive operation is performed with activationCooldown, and the code has no path from external input to a dangerous use of this variable. Hence the claim of a hard‑coded credential vulnerability is unfounded.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: activationCooldown is set to a hardcoded value
finding.assumptions: The activationCooldown variable is hardcoded and not configurable, which might lead to predictable behavior.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code fragment does not contain any OS command execution functions such as system(), exec(), popen(), or similar. The variable activationCooldown is a plain double initialized to a hard‑coded value 1.0 and subsequently decremented in a numeric expression (line 111). There is no construction or invocation of a command string based on untrusted data. Therefore the claimed OS Command Injection cannot occur.
